summary: Lets pooled SaaS users sign in with a global Cloud identity provider and enter an organization only after authenticated membership checks.
userImpact: The neutral organization finder offers configured Cloud account sign-in methods alongside email and organization-name discovery, with a separate account-creation link; existing personal-email accounts can use the one-time email-link fallback.
After Cloud sign-in, one active organization opens automatically; multiple active memberships require an explicit organization choice.
configuration: Cloud account identity remains opt-in; tenant-specific login policies and DNS-verified discovery domains are unchanged.

changes: The global Cloud identity-provider start endpoint accepts the exact /login return path in addition to /cloud/onboarding.

security: The provider callback return path remains exact and signed; organization entry rechecks an authenticated active membership and issues a tenant-bound session.
No account or tenant is selected from an unverified email alone, and email-only account merging remains disabled.
documentation: The technical SSO guide describes identity-first Cloud account sign-in and authenticated organization selection.
knownLimitations: A work-email domain shared by multiple organizations cannot automatically identify one tenant before authentication.
rollback: Redeploy the prior OSS host images; existing tenant discovery and Cloud onboarding sign-in remain available and no database rollback is needed.
validation: Frontend and browser tests cover global provider presentation, sole-tenant entry, multiple-membership selection, and failure handling.
PostgreSQL identity integration verifies the signed /login callback, membership-gated tenant switch, and sibling denial.
